# `list.push` mutates its receiver and returns it, and Go's append does only
# the second — so the intrinsic carries the in-place half by rendering the
# assignment to its own receiver. That is right where the result is discarded
# and invalid anywhere else: `xs = xs.push(v)`, which the method's return type
# invites, emitted `m.xs = m.xs = append(m.xs, v)` and would not compile. It
# never has, in a handler or a component method.

sngl generate --lang=go --platform=bubbletea --out=out app.sngl
exists out/model.go

# A discarded result is one assignment, as before.
grep 'm.bare = append\(m.bare, "b"\)' out/model.go

# An assignment to the receiver itself is also one: the intrinsic already made
# it, so the program's adds nothing.
grep 'm.same = append\(m.same, "s"\)' out/model.go
! grep 'm.same = m.same = ' out/model.go

# A different target keeps both halves: the receiver is mutated, then the
# target binds it. Dropping either would lose what the declaration says.
grep 'm.src = append\(m.src, "x"\)' out/model.go
grep 'm.dst = m.src' out/model.go

# Nothing anywhere emits a doubled assignment.
! grep '= m.[a-z]* = ' out/model.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

component main {
    var (
        bare list<string> = []
        same list<string> = []
        src list<string> = []
        dst list<string> = []
    )

    button(text="1", @click { bare.push("b") })
    button(text="2", @click { same = same.push("s") })
    button(text="3", @click { dst = src.push("x") })
    text #out(value=string(bare.length()))
}
